ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, limited partners and individuals with significant control against FINTRAC enforcement actions and PCMLTFA record-keeping rules; domestic and foreign PEPs and heads of international organizations are subject to enhanced due diligence per FINTRAC guidance; include screening against UN Security Council consolidated lists, Canadian sanctions lists under the United Nations Act and Special Economic Measures Act, and OFAC SDN lists as routine banking and marketplace compliance practice; identity verification and beneficial-ownership verification at or above 25% is compulsory; a low-risk licence-exempt digital publisher may use streamlined customer due diligence, but source-of-funds, ownership-chain and immigration-status documents remain mandatory for the partnership record.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada) using the NUANS automated name search and, where applicable, the provincial limited partnership registry portal (e.g., ServiceOntario Business Registry) for extra-provincial LP declaration filing.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Canada Business Corporations Act and applicable LP declaration rules, names must not be deceptively similar to any existing registered corporate, business or trademark name and must follow federal/provincial naming regulations. Federal names may be in English, French or bilingual; where the entity transacts in Quebec, the limited partnership designation must appear in French ('société en commandite' / 's.e.c.'); transliteration of non-Latin-script owner names is required using established Canadian transliteration practice. The name must contain a legal element identifying the entity as a limited partnership.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: bank, banque, banker, banking (Bank Act, S.C. 1991, c. 46, s. 973 – ministerial consent required)
insurance, assurance, insurer, reinsurance (OSFI or provincial regulator consent required)
trust, loan, loan and trust (federal trust-company consent required)
university, college, institute (educational authority consent may be required in certain provinces)
royal, crown, federal, municipal, ministerial (suggesting Crown or government connection – prohibited absent consent)
canada, canadian, national, international (use restricted by federal name policy and provincial name disclosure conditions)
limited partnership, limited, l.p., s.e.c., société en commandite (mandatory LP designation element)
cooperative, co-operative, condo, condominium (restricted under cooperative and condominium statutes)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection the applicant may (1) file a rebuttal within the reserved 90-day window based on corrected factual evidence or the written consent of the conflicting nameholder; (2) submit a revised NUANS report or a variation of the rejected name without paying a new search fee if filed within the same reservation period; (3) request a name review from the Director of Corporations Canada under the CBCA (normally within 12 months of rejection) and thereafter appeal the Director's final decision to the Federal Court under s. 241 of the CBCA. For a provincial LP rejection, the equivalent administrative review is filed through the provincial registry (e.g., name-review form at ServiceOntario) within 90 days, followed by judicial review before the provincial superior court; legal counsel should manage the preparation of consents, disclaimers and supporting exemptions.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is accepted for administrative, mail-forwarding and bookkeeping purposes in the asset-light hyper-casual gaming sector, but cannot serve as the statutory registered office where legal process must be served in person; a physical Canadian address or the office of a licensed registered agent must be open during business hours and evidenced in the registry filings. The registered office must remain at a fixed Canadian address within the registering jurisdiction.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low. Estimated annual likelihood of unannounced physical inspection is under 5% for a low-risk, licence-exempt digital publisher with no cash handling and no consumer-facing physical presence; the probability rises to a 20–30% range only if CRA tax audit triggers, FINTRAC compliance examination, or AML/sanctions enforcement events materialize.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada has no federal limited partnership statute. The Limited Partnership is constituted under provincial law (e.g., Ontario Limited Partnerships Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. L.2, ss. 2, 7, 9, 15; Alberta Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c. P-3). Federal recognition for extra-provincial registration and tax accounts is obtained through Corporations Canada under the Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 9-10, 23 and through Canada Revenue Agency Business Registration. Provincial filing fees apply and are not federal fees.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Provincial limited partnership registry (e.g., ServiceOntario Companies and Partnerships Branch) for primary registration; Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada, for extra-provincial registration of a corporate general partner; Canada Revenue Agency Business Registration Online for federal tax accounts.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Limited Partnership Declaration (Form 1 under provincial Limited Partnerships Act) and, where applicable, Statement of Registration / Extra-Provincial Registration through Corporations Canada.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is imposed by Canadian federal law. The Limited Partnership Agreement determines capital contributions, which may be cash, property, or a promise to contribute, and no statutory escrow account is required. Limited partners retain liability protection only while capital contributions are substantively made and not withdrawn, and provided they do not take part in control of the partnership.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED: The subscription of the Initial Limited Partners to the Limited Partnership Agreement of [●] LP, as set forth in the Capital Contribution Schedule attached to the LP Agreement, is accepted; the General Partner will cause all required formation filings to be made.

RESOLVED FURTHER: The registered office of the Limited Partnership is established at [full address], Province of [●], Canada, and the records are to be maintained there or at another registered records location adopted in writing.

RESOLVED FURTHER: [Name A] is appointed Chief Executive Officer, [Name B] Chief Financial Officer, and [Name C] Corporate Secretary, each to serve until the General Partner removes or replaces the officer.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial limited partnership registry (e.g., ServiceOntario Companies and Partnerships Branch) and authorized NUANS search house accredited by Corporations Canada where extra-provincial registration is sought.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request for '[●] Limited Partnership' or '[●] LP'. Attach a NUANS Name Search Report dated within 90 days, ensure the suffix clearly indicates limited liability, and obtain written consent if the name relies on regulated or personal names.
required_dossiers: NUANS Name Search Report dated within 90 days
Consent to name use from the named individual or entity, if applicable
Certificate of Status or registry search for the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If refused, submit alternative names through the same registry or appeal to the Director under the relevant Limited Partnerships Act within 15 days, attaching a revised NUANS report.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute the Limited Partnership Agreement and Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel, notary or commissioner of oaths; provincial limited partnership registry for prescribed form.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Limited Partnership Agreement covering capital accounts, profit/loss allocation, management authority of the general partner, admission and withdrawal of partners, transfer restrictions, dissolution and dispute resolution. Execute the Limited Partnership Declaration (Form 1) before a commissioner of oaths or notary.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Status of general partner
Registered office address and landlord consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry requires more specificity, file an amended declaration or supplementary schedule within 30 days, clarifying the prescribed particulars and contribution amounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the Declaration and Obtain Certificate of Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial limited partnership registry; ServiceOntario dedicated filing window or online portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pay the applicable provincial filing fee and submit the executed Limited Partnership Declaration with the registered office address. Obtain a numbered or certified acknowledgement of registration and verify the effective date of formation.
required_dossiers: Approved NUANS report and name reservation certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is queried, cure the deficiency by filing a correction statement or re-submitting the Declaration within 30 days; request expedited handling where delay would cause prejudice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Federal Tax Accounts with the Canada Revenue Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency Business Registration Online (CRA BRO) and federal tax services.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the provincial certificate of registration to obtain a federal Business Number. Apply for GST/HST registration if the partnership makes taxable supplies of software services, register a Payroll account once employees are hired, and maintain the partnership in CRA records for filing T5013 Partnership Information Return. The pass-through tax classification requires each partner to report allocations on their own returns.
required_dossiers: General partner's business number and CRA access code
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA registration is delayed or queried, contact the CRA Business Enquiries line, provide the requested documents, and amend the registration through the Business Registration Online correction function.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Annual Returns and Maintain Registered Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial companies and partnerships branch; CRA for federal tax filing; Corporations Canada for extra-provincial annual returns.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Maintain an annual calendar for provincial limited partnership filings, CRA T5013 return and information filings, and extra-provincial annual returns where applicable. Keep at the registered office: the executed declaration, partnership agreement, capital account records, minutes/consents of the general partner, and CRA confirmation. Update changes in general partner status, registered office, or partnership name promptly.
required_dossiers: General partner consent to continued registration
Updated partnership records and capital account ledger
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an annual filing is rejected or a late-filing penalty is imposed, file the delinquent return with payment of the late fee, and if the partnership has been struck, apply for reinstatement or revival before the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Assess Post-Registration Physical, Zoning, and Occupational Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal licensing office, employment and occupational health authority, and local building/fire safety jurisdiction.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm whether the hyper-casual games studio operates as a pure software publisher with no physical manufacturing. If an office is established, obtain a municipal business licence, verify zoning compliance of the leased premises, complete occupancy inspection, register as an employer under the provincial workers' compensation authority, and conduct a workplace hazard assessment.
required_dossiers: Fire safety inspection report under the National Fire Code
Employer registration with provincial workers' compensation authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If municipal licensing or zoning approval is refused, appeal to the local council, planning advisory committee, or zoning board of adjustment; alternatively submit a revised seating/occupancy plan or relocation certificate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada – Digital Technologies Branch; provincial labour and occupational health authority (where applicable); municipal licensing office for business premises.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — software publishing of mobile games is not a federally licensed activity; only an ordinary municipal business licence is required for the office premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada; provincial environmental ministry (e.g., Ontario Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no physical manufacturing or point-source discharge; office-based hyper-casual game publishing does not trigger a full Environmental Impact Assessment under the Impact Assessment Act S.C. 2019, c. 28, s. 1 or provincial EIA equivalents.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for industrial effluent; compliance with municipal sewer and water bylaws is required. Office waste, including electronics, must be handled under provincial e-waste rules and workplace volatile organic compound limits under occupational health and safety regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the National Fire Code of Canada 2020 must be obtained through the local fire marshal for office premises; structural load and occupancy certification under the National Building Code of Canada 2020 is required; occupational clearance is confirmed through the provincial occupational health and safety authority, employer registration with the workers' compensation board, and any required application for a workplace harassment/violence prevention program.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); online portal: My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident limited partnership must file Form RC4601 (Non-Resident Income Tax Return) or Form RC4973 if carrying on business in Canada, and register for a Business Number (BN) via CRA's Business Registration Online (BRO) service. For GST/HST, the partnership obtains a separate GST/HST account number under the same BN if it makes taxable supplies in Canada and is not a small supplier. Application requires partnership agreement, general partner identification, Canadian representative (if no permanent establishment), and proof of non-resident status.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Limited partnership is fiscally transparent under section 96 of the Income Tax Act (Canada); each partner computes share of income/loss. No check-the-box regime exists federally; however, a partnership may elect under section 216(4) for non-resident partner income from property, and hybrid mismatch rules apply under subsection 18.1(1) and Part XII considerations for foreign-owned partnerships; GST/HST election under section 150 of the Excise Tax Act can be made to have closely related entities file combined returns where applicable.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) / Harmonized Sales Tax (HST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 annual worldwide taxable supplies (including exempt supplies disregarded for small supplier determination); once exceeded, mandatory GST/HST registration, unless the non-resident is engaged in a commercial activity and does not meet the small supplier threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate real-time e-invoicing or fiscal clearance; GST/HST registrants must issue prescribed information on invoices (section 169 and 221 of the Excise Tax Act). Business-to-business electronic data interchange and EDI/API-based systems are voluntary. No digital stamping or pre-clearance requirement exists at the federal level for invoices; however, all records must be retained in Canada or made available electronically to CRA on request.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under sections 123(1)(f)(iii) and 167(1) of the Excise Tax Act for supplies of services exported to non-residents, including digital advertising monetization services provided to non-resident ad networks/publishers, provided the supply is made to a non-resident and the service is not performed in connection with real property situated in Canada, tangible personal property located in Canada, or a service rendered to persons present in Canada. Hyper-casual game publishing services delivered remotely to non-resident advertising platforms (AdMob, AppLovin) qualify as zero-rated exports if the recipient is a non-resident and is not registered for GST/HST.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (Form B13A) or Electronic Export Report via Canadian International Trade Single Window (CBSA ASL)
Inward Remittance Certificate or wire transfer proof from AdMob/AppLovin payout
Contract or service agreement evidencing offshore supply
GST/HST zero-rated supply invoice containing buyer’s country and non-resident status
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess a zero-rated supply within the normal reassessment period (4 years; 3 years for most corporations) and apply section 33.1 of the Income Tax Act for transfer pricing penalties up to 10% of net transfer pricing adjustment for cross-border service payments. Penalties under section 280 of the Excise Tax Act for knowingly making false statements in a return are the greater of CAD 250 and 50% of the net tax evaded. Fraudulent export zero-rating claims attract penalty under section 327(1) of the Excise Tax Act (CAD 10,000 or 100% of evaded tax) and possible criminal prosecution under section 239 of the Income Tax Act (up to 200% of tax evaded, imprisonment up to 5 years). Clawback of input tax credits and reinstatement of 5% GST plus applicable provincial HST component may apply to the full consideration of any mischaracterized supply.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (monetary authority and foreign exchange reserves); Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for federal bank prudential regulation; Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for AML/counter-terrorist financing supervision; Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) for Investment Canada Act review. Canada has no central foreign exchange control administration or surrender authorization.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible and Canada maintains International Monetary Fund Article VIII obligations. Both current account and capital account transactions are generally free from exchange control approval mechanisms. Profit remittance and capital repatriation from a Canadian Limited Partnership are unrestricted in form or amount, subject to Canadian tax withholding obligations under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act on certain payments made to non-residents, any applicable income tax treaty reductions, and transaction-level FINTRAC reporting. Non-resident investment attracting control of a Canadian business may require notification or a net-benefit review under the Investment Canada Act; hyper-casual game publishing is not regarded as a regulated cultural industry for ICA purposes unless a distinct Canadian heritage or cultural business element is acquired. The practical hurdles are not exchange control but KYC/bank compliance, tax characterization of limited partnership income, and the need for a Canadian registered office and named agent.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada does not impose export proceeds surrender requirements. There is no statutory timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or designated window within which export receipts must be converted into Canadian dollars. Export receipts can be retained in any permitted foreign currency, offset against payables or hedged privately, and converted at the commercial bank's prevailing rate. Reporting obligations are indirect only: FINTRAC monitors large cash and electronic funds transactions (C$10,000 or more) and suspicious transactions; Statistics Canada may require Balance of Payments reporting for merchandise and digital-services export receipts when Canadian transactors exceed prescribed thresholds. For a Canadian LP distributing hyper-casual games through foreign ad networks, the USD revenue stream can remain in USD accounts without any surrender or conversion obligation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low-Medium as primary treasury; Medium as a supplementary collection or vendor-payment rail. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise Business, Airwallex, Payoneer, Currenxie) are not authorized Canadian deposit-taking institutions under the Bank Act, are not CDIC-insured, and generally cannot provide a Canadian personal or corporate clearing number for LVTS purposes. An EMI that accepts Canadian-dollar funds or executes remittances in Canada must itself be registered as a Money Services Business with FINTRAC and maintain Canadian AML program obligations; many offshore EMIs either avoid Canadian-domiciled clients or restrict access to Schedule I bank-linked funding. They may nonetheless be used for receipt collection from AdMob/AppLovin via USD virtual accounts, but all treasury balances should be swept daily to a Schedule I bank account through a compliant EFT/wire path. Do not rely on an offshore EMI for regulatory capital, intercompany loan servicing, or tax filings; the Canadian LP must retain a domestic Schedule I bank for statutory title, audit evidence, and treasury credibility.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and FINTRAC guidance, Canadian banks may accept risk-based remote onboarding, but for a limited partnership with non-resident limited partners and cross-border ad-tech revenue, the practical default is that at least one director or authorized signatory with substantive authority must attend an in-person KYC interview at a Canadian branch, or must complete a bank-specific video-notarized session with a Canadian-licensed lawyer. Some institutions allow remote opening with a foreign-notarized corporate resolution and apostille where the beneficial ownership is simple and low risk, but hyper-casual gaming receivables from multiple ad networks are frequently treated as higher monitoring intensity, making a physical branch visit necessary. Additional face-to-face verification is commonly required for Canadian Registered Agent identity, proof of address, source of initial capital, and the bank mandate authorizing any US-dollar clearing instructions. A strictly remote-only onboarding for this LP structure is generally not viable with Tier 1 Canadian banks unless the transaction qualifies for a limited 'premium business banking' exception.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The business appears to be a money service business or payment intermediary because of aggregated payouts from AdMob and AppLovin, with high-frequency USD incoming wires.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed publisher and receiver agreements with Google AdMob and AppLovin; monthly payout reports from both networks for the first 12 months; app store publisher dashboard screenshots showing held-title game applications; unit economic model and revenue attribution to the LP; a notarized declaration that the LP does not act for third-party funds and has no MSB business intent; and a bank-supported transaction flow summary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Limited partnership structure with one or more foreign limited partners obscures ultimate beneficial ownership and source of wealth.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the limited partnership registration and partnership agreement; full schedule of all partners with ID pages, due diligence questionnaires, source-of-wealth statements and, where requested, bank references; FATCA/CRS self-certification forms (Form W-8BEN-E / CRS Partner Self-Certification) for each non-resident partner; corporate chart and ultimate beneficial owner diagram; explanations for any prior corporate dissolution or name change.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Low physical substance in Canada with no dedicated office or payroll.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered office agreement with a Canadian corporate-services provider; Canadian registered agent acknowledgment; signed resolutions of general partner appointing a Canadian-resident authorized signatory; leases or co-working agreements if any; evidence of management activities being carried on in Canada (board packs, IP licensing agreement of the game portfolio to the Canadian LP, server and development hosting agreements); and future Canadian hiring/payroll plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large expected USD volume from foreign ad networks into CAD accounts, creating potential measured transaction exposure and unusual velocity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 12-month cash-flow projection breaking out expected gross ad revenue, ad network payout cycles, platform commissions, SDK licensing fees, and net treasury requirements; treasury management policy describing daily sweeps and FX hedging board approval; counterparty onboarding list for AdMob, AppLovin, Unity Ads, and Vungle; historical payout records (if any); and an explanation of any commingled development-cost recovery from related entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital contribution arrives via multiple foreign-wire transfers from individual founders or from an offshore parent, appearing as third-party funding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Contribution schedule matched to the limited partnership agreement; each capital call notice and bank wire instruction bearing the LP's name and 'Capital Contribution' purpose; authenticated wire confirmations; a table identifying the source of funds (savings, salary, sale of equity, corporate dividend) with supporting tax filings or brokerage statements; a signed statutory declaration from each contributor confirming no money laundering or unlawful proceeds; and independent legal opinion - if the bank requires - confirming the limited partner's entitlement to make contributions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a Canadian LP, inbound capital injections are executed as SWIFT MT103 wire payments to the bank account of the partnership. Canada imposes no official 'purpose code' list comparable to certain Asian regimes, but the remittance field should use an explicit instruction such as 'Capital contribution to Canadian Limited Partnership CA-LP; not for export proceeds; no FX surrender required.' The bank's compliance team will rely on free-format OCR and call-report fields; use a precise Reference for Account or Beneficiary Information field with the LP legal name and capital call number. Direct routing should be via a correspondent relation: USD wires to Canadian banks are usually routed through each bank's New York/US clearing post (RBC via RBC Bank, TD via TD Bank in the US, etc.), with final settlement to CAD or to an omnibus USD account at the Canadian bank. If the LP is using a dedicated 'Capital Escrow/Contribution Account', the general partner should first sign a written escrow or capital call instruction and then wire same-day to the operational account. FINTRAC large notification is handled by the bank for C$10,000+ EFTs; the LP is nevertheless required to have its own AML records when it acts as a financial intermediary, which it does not. Non-resident direct investment triggers no exchange approval but may require Investment Canada Act notification or review if certain ownership thresholds are crossed; for hyper-casual games, the applicable review threshold as of 2025 for a WTO investor is C$5.0 billion enterprise value, while acquisition of a 'cultural business' still carries a lower net-benefit test, so an independent legal memorandum on ICA applicability should be included in the treasury opening pack.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for cross-border trade settlements are dominated by (a) SWIFT MT103 via SWIFT gpi for high-value and medium-value payments to suppliers, contractors, SDK licensors, and overseas studios; (b) ACH or wire-based clearing for low-value recurring digital services; and (c) documentary Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700) for large fixed-amount purchases of intellectual property/studio assets or master licenses where supplier terms demand payment against presentation of documents. For a hyper-casual game publisher, Commercial LC utilisation is rare and typically limited to one-off licensing acquisition of an entire game catalogue from a foreign entity; in such cases the Canadian bank will issue an irrevocable LC to the foreign studio with CIP/CIF or similar delivery terms and an SWIFT MT103/MT202 final settlement. Recurring disbursements such as ad-network SDK fees, cloud hosting, code-signing services, and freelance artist payments should be cleared via a US-dollar account maintained at the Canadian bank, with Fedwire/CHIPS for same-day USD needed, or via a CAD SWIFT MT103 for counterparties without USD accounts. No cryptocurrency or private stablecoin rails are permissible in the primary treasury; Canadian banks will not clear digital-asset transactions for corporate accounts without enhanced OSFI-defined due diligence and likely exclusion. All outgoing MT103s must carry transparent purpose codes such as 'SDK License Fees', 'Software Development Services', 'Cloud Hosting Services', or 'IP Acquisition', matching underlying agreements, to avoid downstream correspondent bank holds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD spot and outright forward contracts with a Canadian Schedule I bank under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and Credit Support Annex; the underlying exposure must be a forecasted USD revenue stream from AdMob/AppLovin, documented through a board-approved treasury policy.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies that are not freely deliverable in Canadian clearing channels, such as CNY and INR, where the central bank of the relevant jurisdiction restricts onshore deliverable forward access for foreign investors; NDF payouts settle in CAD or USD.

Cross-currency swaps (XCCY) between US dollars and Canadian dollars for balance sheet matching of converted intercompany loans or capital-account contributions, executed with the bank's global markets desk under the ISDA/CEM structure.
Vanilla over-the-counter FX options (call/put) on CAD/USD, including zero-premium collars or risk reversals, to hedge against adverse USD depreciation of monthly ad-network remittances.
Instruments denominated as 'flexible forwards' with window delivery dates, allowing the LP to absorb the daily volatility of game revenue while guaranteeing a worst-case conversion rate.
No leveraged FX speculation or binary-products are permissible; the hedging programme must be strictly linked to underlying cash-flow forecasts and supported by monthly management reporting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee of CAD 100; continued failure for two consecutive years may result in administrative strike-off and loss of limited liability protection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Five months after the end of the LP's fiscal period; for a December 31 year-end, due May 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 30 per day, minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500, plus daily compound interest on any unpaid balance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Three months after the end of the LP's fiscal year; for a December 31 year-end, due March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 5% of the balance outstanding plus 1% per month for up to 12 months; repeat omissions may invoke CRA prosecution and trust fund sanctions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the anniversary of the LP's registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative cancellation of registration after one year of continuous non-compliance; the general partner's liability may become unlimited during any period of default.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No federal statutory audit is mandatory for a private limited partnership; audit becomes compulsory if the LP is a reporting issuer under provincial securities law, if the partnership agreement or a major creditor requires it, or if the LP is a public or regulated entity.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable LPs; otherwise Canadian ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) as local GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The LP must maintain a current register of ultimate beneficial owners; an annual confirmation is required to verify that any partner holding 25% or more of the partnership capital or control remains correctly identified and to report transfers to the registered agent and Corporations Canada within 30 days of the transfer.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 – USD 15,000 for a private hyper-casual gaming LP with IFRS/ASPE financial statements
